H70: WHAT ARRIVAL CLUSTERING ALONE COSTS THE TAIL. Apple M4.
Run 2026-11-18 17:38 IST. Thresholds fixed before the run;
the registration is in docs/experiments.md. Verdicts recorded 2026-11-18, below.

OS      : ProductVersion 27.2, BuildVersion 26B123

SATURATED LINES: 1

================================================================================
UTILISATION, WHICH SCOPES EVERYTHING BELOW
================================================================================

The full path saturates between 10,000,000 and 15,000,000 messages per second
on this machine: every earlier sweep records saturated=0 at 10,000,000 and
saturated=1 at 15,000,000, for all three wait strategies. This run offered
5,000,000, so it ran at roughly one third to one half of capacity. Every
verdict below is a statement about that operating point and not about the
system at its limit.

================================================================================
VERDICTS
================================================================================

H70 (a) BURSTINESS INFLATES THE TAIL AT A FIXED MEAN RATE.          REFUTED
    Registered: p99.9 at branching 0.8 at or above 2.0 times p99.9 at
    branching 0.0, with 21 of 30 on the paired sign test.
    Measured, p99.9 ratio by wait strategy:
        spin  1.0060   at or above 2.0 in  1/30   sign 16/30  p = 0.856
        isb   0.9872   at or above 2.0 in  2/30   sign 17/30  p = 0.585
        wfe   1.0285   at or above 2.0 in  1/30   sign 20/30  p = 0.099
    Not one wait strategy reaches the threshold and not one reaches
    significance. The registered effect is absent, and absent by a factor of
    two, not by a margin.

H70 (b) THE INFLATION GROWS WITH THE BRANCHING RATIO.               REFUTED
    Registered: median p99.9 ordered 0.0 below 0.5 below 0.8 in at or above 24
    of 30 launches. Measured: 5 of 30 for spin, isb and wfe alike, which is
    what chance alone produces from three interchangeable arms.

H70 (c) THE MEDIAN IS ALMOST UNTOUCHED.                             SUPPORTED
    p50 ratio 0.8 against 0.0: 1.0113 spin, 1.0000 isb, 1.0081 wfe, against a
    registered 1.25. THIS IS THE VERDICT THAT MAKES (a) MEAN SOMETHING. The
    arms are not differing in throughput and then being compared on tail; they
    are doing identical work at identical speed, and the clustering still does
    not move the tail.

H70 (d) RANDOMNESS ALONE IS NOT THE EFFECT.    SUPPORTED AT THE REGISTERED
                                               DEPTH, AND THE REGISTRATION
                                               CHOSE THE WRONG DEPTH
    Registered: p99.9 at branching 0.0 within 1.5 times the periodic arm.
    Measured at p99.9: 1.0517 spin, 1.0574 isb, 1.0311 wfe. Passes easily.
    MEASURED AT OTHER DEPTHS, SAME TWO ARMS, SAME LAUNCHES, PAIRED:
        percentile   ratio   sign     p
        50.00        1.292   30/30    1.9e-09
        85.39        1.761   30/30    1.9e-09
        95.73        2.122   30/30    1.9e-09
        98.75        2.535   29/30    5.8e-08
        99.64        2.604   27/30    8.4e-06
        99.89        1.052   22/30    1.6e-02
    The control passed only because p99.9 is the one depth at which the two
    curves have converged. Half a decade earlier the same comparison is 2.12
    times at 30 of 30. The threshold was not wrong; the single quantile it was
    read at was.

H70 (e) THE CURVES ARE RESOLVED WHERE THEY ARE READ.                SUPPORTED
    Minimum observations beyond the p99.9 level: 10,656, against a registered
    100. Two orders of magnitude of margin.

H70 (f) NO ARM SATURATED.                              FAILED ON ONE LINE
                                                       OF ONE THOUSAND EIGHTY
    One line reports saturated=1: launch 25, hawkes_0.5, wait=isb, epoch 2,
    offered 5.002 against achieved 0.421. The registration says a saturating
    arm is dropped and the fact reported rather than the rate lowered until it
    passes. Reported here, and checked rather than argued: each launch is the
    median of its three epochs, so one outlying epoch cannot move its launch
    median unless it is the middle value. Recomputing (a) for isb with launch
    25 removed entirely gives ratio 0.9853 against 0.9872, and 17 of 29
    against 17 of 30. The verdict does not depend on it.

================================================================================
WHAT WAS ACTUALLY FOUND, WHICH IS NOT WHAT WAS REGISTERED
================================================================================

Median microseconds, wait=spin, 30 launches, median across epochs then across
launches:

    survival    percentile   periodic   hawkes 0.0   hawkes 0.5   hawkes 0.8
    5.000e-01      50.00        0.205        0.264        0.265        0.267
    1.461e-01      85.39        0.261        0.460        0.462        0.469
    4.270e-02      95.73        0.311        0.660        0.665        0.680
    1.248e-02      98.75        0.347        0.882        0.892        0.925
    3.646e-03      99.64        0.497        1.296        1.305        1.532
    1.066e-03      99.89        4.358        4.671        4.606        4.648
    9.100e-05      99.99       18.748       20.988       19.480       20.268
    1.000e-06      99.9999     36.256       36.928       36.344       36.280

RESULT 1. CLUSTERING IS ABSORBED COMPLETELY, AT EVERY DEPTH. The ratio of
branching 0.8 to branching 0.0 stays between 0.98 and 1.07 across the whole
curve, with its largest value 1.066 at the 99.64th percentile and no
significance at all past p99.9 (16 of 30, p = 0.86 at p99.9; 17 of 30,
p = 0.59 at p99.9999). Fano factors of 0.900 and 13.920 produce the same
latency distribution. At one third to one half of capacity, this ring and this
book do not care how the arrivals are bunched.

RESULT 2, AND IT IS THE LARGE ONE. RANDOMNESS COSTS UP TO 2.6 TIMES, AND IT
COSTS IT IN THE BODY RATHER THAN THE TAIL. A Poisson schedule against a
perfectly periodic one at the same mean rate: 1.29 times at the median, rising
to 2.60 times at the 99.64th percentile, then collapsing to 1.05 by p99.9 and
to 1.02 in the far tail. All at 30 of 30 or 29 of 30, p below 1e-5, and
reproduced independently under all three wait strategies with ratios within
0.1 of each other.

RESULT 3, METHODOLOGICAL, AND THE REASON THE INSTRUMENT WAS BUILT. The effect
in Result 2 is invisible at p99.9, modest at p50, and maximal between p95 and
p99.6. A registration that reads one quantile can therefore pass a control
that a curve fails by a factor of two. That is what happened here to H70 (d),
in a registration written by the same person who built the CCDF emitter to
avoid exactly this. The seven-point percentile ladder this project reported
before would have caught it at p99 and missed it at p99.9; the choice between
those two is arbitrary and the curve removes the choice.

================================================================================
WHAT THIS RUN CANNOT SETTLE
================================================================================

It cannot say whether clustering is absorbed at a rate near saturation. One
third to one half of capacity leaves room for a burst to drain before the next
one arrives, and the obvious next measurement is the same sweep at 10,000,000
messages per second, the highest rate at which this path has been observed not
to saturate. That is a new registration, not a re-reading of this one.

It cannot say why a random schedule costs what it does, only that it does and
that clustering on top of it does not. A queueing explanation is available and
untested: a periodic schedule never presents two messages at once, while a
Poisson schedule does so constantly, and at half utilisation the queue formed
by a Poisson coincidence drains before a Hawkes burst can add to it.

It is one mean rate, one instrument count, one machine, one feed, and
performance cores only.
